findings.governingReading: Archer is functionally finished or gravely incapacitated.
findings.explanation: The English turns combat incapacity into an ongoing process of death.

findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂の手を引いて真横に跳べば
findings.governingReading: Shirou plans to take Rin’s hand and then jump directly sideways.
findings.explanation: The English changes the hand-taking into moving Rin herself and deletes Shirou’s sideways jump.

findings.highlight: I’m sure I can manage something
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s unfinished “then, with that—” leads directly into his judgment that the concrete maneuver will work.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the specified calculation with vague confidence that he can manage something.

findings.governingReading: The swollen shadow ruptures or bursts.
findings.explanation: “Explodes” adds an explosive mechanism to the source’s rupture.

findings.highlight: tramples over the forest under one breath
findings.governingReading: The shadow overruns the forest in one breath or single sweep.
findings.explanation: “Under one breath” is malformed English and obscures the speed of the action.

findings.highlight: A fatal fever from the tropics
findings.evidenceJa: 熱帯の森に潜む致死の熱病
findings.governingReading: The image is a lethal fever lurking within a tropical forest.
findings.explanation: The English replaces hidden presence in the forest with geographic origin and weakens the predatory metaphor.

findings.evidenceJa: 対抗する[ruby text=ワクチン char=2]手段はなく
findings.governingReading: There is no written “means of countering it,” read specifically as “vaccine.”
findings.explanation: The English keeps only the ruby reading and deletes the broader countermeasure layer.

findings.highlight: my mind dies before my body. abandons my body and dies first.
findings.evidenceJa: 精神が、体より先に死んだ
findings.governingReading: The mind dies before the body after the flesh struggles against the heat.
findings.explanation: The English states the death twice and appends a subjectless contradictory-looking fragment.

findings.governingReading: The flesh has lost its written “soul,” read as “mind/heart.”
findings.explanation: The English preserves only “soul,” erasing the link back to the mind that died first.

findings.evidenceJa: どこかで、産声が聞こえた気がした
findings.governingReading: While dissolving, Shirou feels as though he hears a birth cry somewhere.
findings.explanation: The English page is blank, deleting the distant uncertain sound that closes the bad end.
